title: Field of 68 Efficiency
text:
This scatter plot shows each team in the projected field of 68’s offensive and defensive efficiency. I calculated their efficiencies using formulas found at https://pillars.taylor.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1001&context=sport-management-student-projects, which is a research paper about analyzing basketball. I found the formulas and used them to calculate each team’s efficiency on both sides. The teams that are closest to the top right corner performed the best on both sides and are potential factors in winning the NCAA tournament.

  mutate(
    possesions = field_goals_attempted - offensive_rebounds + turnovers + (0.4 * free_throws_attempted)
  )


efficiency <- possesions |>
  group_by(team_short_display_name) |>
  summarize(
    offensive_efficiency = sum(team_score)/ sum(possesions) *100,

title: Home vs Road Wins
text:
This dumbbell chart shows each team in the projected field of 68’s home versus road wins. Winning games on the road will be extremely important during the NCAA Tournament, as teams do not get to play on their home courts. You might be the home team, but they are all neutral-site games. Being able to see which teams performed better on the road than others can be very helpful in determining who could have won the 2020 NCAA Men’s Tournament. After my three visualizations, I believe Gonzaga or LSU would have been good choices to win the Tournament. Gonzaga had the most wins in total during the season and also performed well on the road. They were also in the middle of the pack for overall efficiency but had the highest offensive efficiency. LSU had the highest total efficiency in both offense and defense and was in the middle, closer to the top, for total wins and road wins.

I am from Filley, NE and went to high school at Freeman Public Schools. For the first two years of my college education I spent time at Southeast Community College in Lincoln. Sports media is a great major for me as I played sports growing up but knew I wasn’t going to play in college. I have also always loved watching sports no matter how big. Sports media allows me to combine my love of watching sports with my knowledge from playing them and hopefully get a career that I am excited about.

title: 2020 NCAA Tournament Projected Field of 68
text:
This bar chart shows a projected field of 68 for the men’s 2020 NCAA Tournament. I calculated their wins for the regular season only, as most did not have any games in their conference tournaments, or they only had one game. There are two sets of teams because, in the NCAA Tournament, there are always automatic qualifiers, who are the conference champions, and then the at-large bids. For the at-large bids, I only used power conference teams, which are from the Big Ten, Big 12, Pac-12 (RIP), SEC, and the Big East. Sometimes there might be another team from outside those conferences to get an at-large bid, but not consistently enough for me to believe they warranted a spot. I know strength of schedule is also an impact on who gets at-large bids, but no team is usually kept out over another power conference team with fewer wins unless they are auto-bids. For the conference champions, I used the few conferences that had a tournament or declared an automatic qualifier before the whole NCAA Tournament was canceled. For other conferences, I just used their regular season champions, and for the few that had a tie, I used their 1 seeds in their tournaments. So with this chart, we can assume that Gonzaga would be the number one overall seed.
